name_note: The species was published as Ruminococcus faecis and is still labelled [Ruminococcus] faecis in NCBI; GTDB places it in Mediterraneibacter.

sentences.text: The type strain of this species is an anaerobic, Gram-positive, non-motile, non-spore-forming coccus isolated from human faeces.
It grows best at 37 degrees Celsius and ferments several substrates including glucose, giving lactic and acetic acids as the main products.
By 16S rRNA gene sequence it is closest to Ruminococcus torques and Ruminococcus lactaris, which is why it was first named Ruminococcus faecis.
The genus Mediterraneibacter, into which it is now placed, was described from an anaerobic stool isolate cultivated by microbial culturomics.
